title: aes-128/aes-192/aes-256, 7 rounds: Rebound known-key distinguisher [MPR+09]

target.description: Seven AES rounds with initial whitening and final MixColumns omitted (Sections2.1,5.2,6.2). Active-byte path4→1→4→16→4→1→4→4; fixed known key throughout.

setting.key_relation: One randomly drawn AES key revealed to the adversary; the key and its derived round subkeys are fixed during pair construction. No related-key oracle and no attacker choice of the key.
setting.key_population: Known random AES key; no weak-key selection.
setting.plaintext_model: Construct two distinct plaintexts with four active bytes at prescribed positions at input and output; the remaining twelve bytes of each difference are zero. Nonzero active differences are not prescribed values.
assumptions: The round construction does not depend on key-schedule relations, so the known-key setting applies to all three standard key lengths.
setting.reference_model: Known-key restricted input/output pair construction compared to forward/inverse oracle queries to an ideal random 128-bit permutation; no secret-key recovery.

time.note: Section5.2 gives about2^24 AES-round computations on average from the final4→1MixColumns transition; Section6.2 andTable1 give the same exponent. Do not normalize to full-encryption units.

data.note: No separate numerical budget is stated for this configuration.

memory.note: Table1 explicitly gives2^16 native memory entries. Section6.2 calls this negligible; that qualitative comparison is retained, not interpreted as zero bytes or a different numerical configuration.

preprocessing.note: No separate numerical budget is stated for this configuration.

success.description: No numerical complete restricted-pair construction or distinguishing-game success is given at the reported average runtime. The rebound final-transition probability and the linearized method’s expected work are not a fixed-budget whole-attack probability.

review.scope: Targeted exact-edition success audit; construction and parameter-specific defining passages, not a new full-paper audit.

components.description: Section5.2 probability for one controlled candidate to pass the final4-to1 active-byte transition. Average2^24 round computations do not specify a fixed-budget success rate.

evidence.locator: PDF pp.2–3 / printed17–18 Table1 andSection2.1; pp.13–14 /28–29 Section5.2; p.16 /31 Section6.2.
evidence.interpretation: Complete20page primary read; Table1 memory2^16 is visually verified. Body negligible-memory wording does not assert zero. Section6.2 generic reference2^48 is source attribution, not an attack cost; later GP10/DFJ12 analyze the restricted birthday task more tightly. This is a constructive distinguisher, not a minimum-active-S-box structural bound; bound is not applicable.

evidence.locator: PDF p.14 /printed29 Section5.2, Extending the Path; p.16 /printed31 Section6.2; pp.10–11 Section4.3 for the linearized method.
evidence.interpretation: No numerical complete restricted-pair construction or distinguishing-game success is given at the reported average runtime. The rebound final-transition probability and the linearized method’s expected work are not a fixed-budget whole-attack probability.

limitations: Native work and table-entry units are retained; no conversion to full AES encryptions or bytes is inferred.
Whole-attack success probability is not quantified in the primary; local transition probabilities and expected candidate counts are not substituted for it.
